ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: neighbours and letters
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The towns near the colony have people with names: a head, an heir, an envoy and a trader. Write to them, or call them, and they remember.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A letter of condolence in a careful hand means more to a tribe than any call could.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
Each town within reach of the colony has a few people the colony knows by name, real people of their own kind kept in the world while they matter: the town's head, a likely heir, an envoy and a known trader. The faces the colony met who went home live among them too: a prisoner it set free, a wounded guest it tended, a camp's leader, a guest of rank, an envoy, a trader who called. Each of them regards the colony, and some of its people, in their own way, remembers what passed between them, grows old, and is followed by someone new when they're gone.
A colonist can write to any of them, or call them on a comms console. The writer sits down at a table to write, a messenger of their people comes to the gate for the letter, and the answer comes back the same way. What the answer says follows who they are and how they see the colony and the one who wrote, and it changes both a little.

li.heading: Who the neighbours are
li.text: The towns within reach are the nearest 4 within 40 world tiles (with none that near, the nearest 2 within 80), and up to 2 more the colony has dealt with however far: one whose people have exchanged letters with the colony, or a people's nearest town when that people remembers the colony for something. Each has four people known by name.

table.li: Role | Who | When they're gone

Head | At a people's seat (their oldest town), their own leader; elsewhere a headman or headwoman, reeve, mayor or administrator by their era | The heir takes the place; at the seat, whoever the game makes leader
Heir | Younger, with the head's family name | Someone new, later
Envoy | A speaker, herald, envoy or liaison by their era | Someone new, later
Trader | Of the kind their caravans bring | Someone new, later

li.after: Up to 10 faces the colony met are kept besides; when there are more, the one with nothing to remember for longest makes way. A town out of reach, a people fallen, or a person gone is let go, unless something passed between them in the last 60 days. Those Rimfolk made for a role grow old: from sixty, about 4% a year die of it, and 1.2 points more for every year after (16% at seventy). A town's card on the region map tells of who now leads.

li.heading: How they regard the colony
li.text: A neighbour's regard starts from their people: a little over half their goodwill, their people's memory of the colony's good turns (up to 30) and wrongs (up to 40, counting for more), a little for a debt the colony owes them (up to 8), and their nature: 6 more for each step of kindness (Kind counts two), 6 less for each of coldness (Abrasive two; Psychopath, Greedy, Jealous and Bloodlust one each). A people at war with the colony is never better than cool. On top comes what passed between them in person, which halves every 90 days without news.

table.li: Regard | In words
60 or more | holds the colony dear
30 to 59 | is warm toward the colony
10 to 29 | is friendly to the colony
-9 to 9 | is civil to the colony
-29 to -10 | is cool toward the colony
-59 to -30 | is wary of the colony
-60 or less | is hostile to the colony

li.after: A colonist is regarded at half of how they see the colony, plus what that colonist did for their people (one and a half times the deed's strength, up to 40), plus their letters and calls. The faces met start warmer: set free 25, tended 18, a guest 12, a camp 10, an envoy 4, a trader or a visitor 3, and more toward the colonist who did it.

li.heading: Writing a letter
li.text: In a town's card on the region map, or on the region window's Peoples under Faces, press Write by someone's name. Pick what for, who writes (the speaker unless you choose someone else) and how. One letter at a time to each person, three letters and calls under way at most, and a wait before writing to the same person for the same thing again.

table.li: What for | When | Wait
Greetings | Always | 6 days
Condolences | A death among their notables in the last 30 days, or their people in hard times (a world event that falls on them) | 10 days, each loss once
A warning | A hard time in the region, raiders at war with them who came at the colony in the last 30 days, or an enemy camp within 12 tiles of their town | 3 days, each threat once
Asking for news | Always | 5 days
An invitation to visit | Not at war | 15 days
Asking for a little help (medicine or food) | Not at war, and they regard the colony at 25 or more | 20 days

li.after: The writer sits at one of the colony's tables, on a chair, for about an hour (else on any chair, else where they stand), between seven in the morning and ten at night, when nothing more pressing calls them; it is practice at Social. A writer who never finds the time in 3 days lets it go. Then a messenger of their people comes to the gate some hours later, by day, and waits; the writer carries the letter out, or after two hours anyone free does. Twice nobody comes out, and the letter is let go. A people at war with the colony is written to through a messenger of a people at peace with both, under a white flag.

li.heading: The answer
li.text: A letter takes 0.4 days plus, for each tile, 0.4 days by a tribe's runner, 0.33 by medieval riders, 0.22 by industrial couriers or 0.12 by spacers (three quarters of a day at least, twelve at most), and they take a quarter of a day to a day and a quarter to answer. How it lands: 0.55 of their regard for the colony, 0.35 of their regard for the writer, 1.5 for each level of the writer's Social above 6 (less below), 6 for each step of their nature, and what it is for (greetings 5, condolences 15, a warning 12, news 5, an invitation 0, help -10, or -25 when their people are in hard times). A call takes 6 off, condolences, greetings or an invitation by hand to a traditional people add 8, the same again within 12 days takes 10 off, and a people at war takes 20 off. Luck moves it up to 22 either way. Their own words follow what lies between the two sides and what happened at their town lately: a favor they owe or a grudge they hold, a family's claim, a debt or a grant, a town just built or taken.

table.li: How it lands | The answer | Their regard | Goodwill
40 or more | Warm | 6 (condolences 8) | 2
12 to 39 | Kind | 3 | 1
Below -40 | A refusal | -2 | 0

li.after: A good answer counts for more by hand on personal matters (greetings, condolences, an invitation: 1.1 times, 1.3 to tribes, medieval folk and a feudal empire) and for less by a call (0.9 on business, 0.7 on personal matters); the writer is regarded half again as much. A warning well taken adds 2 goodwill and is remembered by their people as a good turn; condolences warmly or kindly taken are remembered as mourning with them. Asking for help costs 2 regard either way, and is given on a warm or kind answer only: 4 to 8 medicine (herbal from a tribe, a medieval people or to a colony without industry) or 40 to 65 pemmican, set down with the letter, and their people remember the colony owes them for it. A warm answer from someone who regards the colony at 35 or more now and then brings a gift worth 80 to 160 silver (scaled by the colony's wealth): one time in three, half the time with a warning.

A people at war answers less often (it keeps silent 15% to 60% of the time, the more it hates the colony the more), never warmly, and goodwill moves one step more with a good answer. Its refusal ends with a threat one time in five (a curt answer one in ten), and their raiders come some days after it, as the letter warned. The messenger bringing an answer is set upon on the road now and then (4%, or 15% with enemies of the colony camped or settled near their town) and comes in with a cut, which a colony doctor can tend. Asked for news, they tell of real things: world events in the region or on them, places near their town, a quest of theirs still open, a people they're at war with. Asked to visit, they come some days later and stay 8 to 14 hours by day; a people's leader can't leave the seat and sends the heir or the envoy.

li.heading: A call on the comms console
li.text: With a powered comms console under a clear sky (no solar flare), a colony can call peoples with the means to answer: industrial and later. Tribes and medieval folk are reached by letter only. The caller stands at the console and talks for a while. At their end, it may be the small hours (from ten at night to six in the morning, by their own clock: asleep, 85% of the time), their people may be in trouble (busy, half the time), or they may be away (15%, a people's leader 30%): an aide takes a message and they call back, in the morning, some hours later, or when the trouble allows. The console rings and the caller, or whoever is free nearest it, answers; nobody in three hours (a raid on, everyone busy) and they leave word instead.
li.after: The answer works the same way as a letter's, with what was said shown over the caller's head and in a letter. Words go down the line, things don't: anything an answer sends still comes by courier. A call is quick, but for condolences or a kind word a letter in a hand counts for more, most of all to a traditional people.

li.heading: Talking with outsiders
li.text: With a colonist selected, right-click someone from outside the colony who isn't hostile (a visitor, a trader, a guest, someone of a camp, a messenger, an envoy, a quest's lodger) and pick "Talk with...". Right-clicking a hostile stays the game's attack. The colonist walks over, the other stops and faces them, and they talk: a short scene of two to six lines said in turn over their heads as bubbles, at a pace to read them. Someone asleep, down, fleeing, on their way out, trading, carrying someone or with danger about won't stop, nor will anyone who regards the colonist at -40 or less or the colony at -60 or less. Each thing has a wait before the same two do it again; some wait for the outsider whoever asks.

table.li: Thing | What comes of it | Wait
Chat | A conversation about what is going on now; a word that warms or cools them both | 6 hours

Ask about their home | Real news in bubbles, kept under the town's Heard lately: what their people are short of, a caravan of theirs on its way, world events, places near their town, a quest of theirs, their wars | a day, anyone
Share a meal, or a drink | Both eat (or drink) the game's own way, the best of the stores each would have by their own food policy, diet and beliefs | 10 hours, 8 for a drink
Give a gift | Fetched from the stores and handed over; it goes home with them, not for sale | 2 days
Put in a good word | Their town's head (else its heir or envoy) hears it once they're home | 5 days, anyone
Carry a letter home | The letters' window, written as usual and handed to them instead of a messenger | a day
Teach for an hour | At a bench of the skill's work, else side by side | 2 days, anyone
Bring something next time | Their people's next visit brings it | 3 days, anyone; one for each people
Invite to stay | They join the colony, if they want to | 3 days, anyone
Get to know them, court them, talk faith | A bond over visits; sweethearts, then lovers; faith closer or debated | 12 hours, a day, a day

li.after: How a talk goes: 0.3 of how they regard the colonist, 0.2 of how they regard the colony (their people's goodwill and memory, or their own regard as a notable), 8 for each step of how the two get on (three steps at most), 1.2 for each level of the colonist's Social above 6, 4 for each step of their nature, up to 6 for knowing each other, and what it is about (a chat 6, news 4, a meal or a drink 10, getting to know them 2, courting -4, faith -2). Luck moves it up to 18 either way: 28 or more is warm, 10 good, -8 plain, -24 cool, below that sour. Each keeps a memory of the other for 12 days (6, 3, nothing, -3, -6), the bond between them moves (8, 4, 1, -3, -6), and the talk runs up to 6, 6, 5, 3 or 2 lines (asked about home, 3 at least; a sour one tells nothing).

Everything is remembered. Someone the colony knows by name takes it into their regard of the colonist (the colony half of it) and remembers it in a line; a stranger is noted and becomes a face the colony knows once home, with the bond carried over. The bond halves in 60 days; a talk more than two days after the last starts a new visit. Two become friends from away with a bond of 35, knowing each other at 30, over two visits or more (12 opinion each for 60 days). Courting needs both drawn to each other, faiths that allow it and knowing each other at 15; it goes by the game's own romance chance, 60% to 100% of it as they know each other better. The first yes makes them sweethearts (15), and two visits later, with a bond of 45, they become lovers the game's own way.

A gift is a share of a stack worth about 120 silver, or one thing. It counts 1.5 times when it suits them (a drink for one with a taste for it, a book for a scholar, a weapon for a fighter, medicine for a healer or a people in hard times, silver or art for the greedy, cloth for a crafter), twice when it suits them and is fine work, and not at all against their beliefs or diet (they hand it back). It warms them by its worth over 12, less from a richer colony (1 to 20), and their people count it as the game counts a gift, at half (up to three quarters when it suits). A good word needs them to regard the colony at 20 and the colonist at 10, and moves their notable 2 to 10; a favour needs 5 (something brought, 15) and no dislike of the one asking. A lesson needs them to know the skill to 6, three levels better than the colonist, and teaches 0.08 to 0.25 experience a tick for an hour; their people remember the colony owes them. Brought next time: worth 60 silver, up to 160 the better they regard the colony, by the next of their people to come once the one who promised has gone home, a day or more later; nobody in 30 days and it lapses.

An invitation needs a reason to stay (love or family here, hard times at home, the colony's faith, a friend here): 12%, 18% more for each reason, 15% less for each tie at home, 0.3% for each point of regard for the colony and the colonist, 1% for each Social level above 6, between 2% and 85%. Their people lose 4 goodwill (2 with two reasons or more). Hospitality's guests are left to Hospitality, and a caravan's trader stays with the caravan. Talking faith (Ideology) with someone of the same faith brings them closer; with another, a debate softens them a little, ends in agreeing to differ, or hardens both, by words, certainty and luck: the game's own certainty moves a little, never a change of faith.

li.heading: Patience, and asking twice
li.text: Someone from outside has patience for a few real things with the colony on a visit, whoever of the colony asks: 3, one more when they regard the colony at 30 or more, another at 60, one more with a friend in the colony and one for a kind nature, one less for a cold one, one less when they regard the colony below 0 and another at -30, between 1 and 6. Each thing done with them uses one; hard words, a challenge and a letter handed over use none. Patience comes back one thing every 12 hours for someone who stays, and in full on a new visit (nothing done with them for two days). The right-click menu says how much they have left ("is glad of the company", "has time for a little more", "has time for one more thing", "has had enough talk for now"), and with none left the things that need it are greyed.
li.after: The asks (news of home, a good word, a lesson, a favour, an invitation, getting to know them, courting, faith) asked again within their wait are marked "asked already": the colonist may still go, and gets "You asked me that already" (or that another colonist did) and nothing more, though it uses their patience. A colonist who asks a third thing within 6 hours is pushy: 4 off the bond between them and 1.5 off a notable's regard of the colonist, and they say so first. Gifts on one visit count for less and less, from anyone: in full, then a half, a third, a quarter; from the fourth on a gift leaves no memory of its own.

li.heading: Talks of their own
li.text: A colonist and someone from outside within 6 cells and in sight of each other, both free (idle, at leisure, eating, passing by), sometimes start a conversation by themselves: 3.5% each look, every 250 ticks, by the colonist's Social (0.7 times at 0, 1.5 at 20, more with a passion), their warmth, a kind nature (1.3) or a shy (0.5), cold (0.6) or abrasive one (0.9); 1.4 times when both linger and half in passing; more when the outsider is kind or likes the colonist, less when they don't; times the setting, a quarter at most. An outsider talks this way at most once every 4 hours and 4 times a visit, the same two once every 12 hours, and a colonist starts one at most once an hour, besides the colony's other talk (so the game's own chitchat stays the bulk). Never with danger about, with a child, with someone leaving, trading or busy, nor with someone who has had enough.
li.after: Such a talk runs 3 lines in passing and up to 6 lingering, by how it goes, only in bubbles. It counts as half a chat: half the regard and bond, half the knowing each other, and a memory only when it goes warmly or sours; nothing at all if they part before it's said.

li.heading: What they talk about
li.text: Each conversation is a piece chosen by what is true right now, the newest news first: their town and its people by name (a new head, a death, someone ill, letters exchanged), the land and the weather they came through, what they're short of, their traders on the way, places near their town; their people's wars and peace as the game's relations have them (whoever set them), and fighting seen on the colony's land; the world's events running or just over, and the conditions over the land; the colony's own news (a raid and who came, a death, a birth, a wedding, a newcomer, a decree, the speaker chosen, a camp, the harvest, the stores) and its hospital once it has a name, with the doctor people trust most; what their people remember the colony for; what is owed between the two sides (a favor their people owe, a good word promised, their family's claim on someone who joined the colony, silver the colony owes, fealty either way, their grudge for their dead or a colonist's vendetta against them) and what became of it; what happened at their town and to them lately (a town just built, taken or made the colony's vassal, a world event begun or over there); how their people's age stands to the colony's; their town's fortune and the world event that moved it; and their own lives (work, family, faith). Each people speaks in its own way. The same piece isn't said to the same person again while another fits, and two who just talked of something drift to another subject.
li.after: What is said is kept. News goes into the town's Heard lately, under its people in the town's card on the region map, with who told whom and when. Talks leave marks the same two pick up later, with what became of it since: the war they asked about over, the sick notable recovered or dead, someone new leading. Only what matters comes as a message or a letter: a promise made (a good word, something brought), an invitation accepted, a courtship answered, a new friend, hard words, a duel, an injury, or a thing that couldn't be done.

li.heading: Bouts, hard words and duels
li.text: A practice bout is fists only: they agree half the time, 12% more for each step of a fighting temper (bloodlust, brawler, abrasive, volatile; kind and wimp less) and 2% for each level they lead at melee, between 5% and 95%, and less from someone who dislikes the colonist. Eight swings each at most; a swing lands at their melee hit chance against the other's dodge (15% to 95%), a blow of 1 to 2.5, and someone hurting at 0.2 gives it up. Each swing is 15 melee experience, 25 if it lands. One bout in 25 (4%, a point more for each step of temper between them, 8% at most) has one blow that goes in harder than meant, 6 to 9, a real injury.
li.after: Hard words leave them insulted (-12 for 15 days), take 12 from the bond and 6 from their regard of the colonist, and their people remember the slight. A fistfight follows at twice the game's own chance after an insult, 14% more for each step of their temper, 5% for each of the colonist's, 5% less for each kind step, 0.2% less for each point they regard the colonist, 70% at most; it is the game's own social fight, and afterwards their people remember it and lose 4 goodwill (never into a war).

A duel of honour is for peoples whose ways know it: tribes, medieval folk, and an empire's titled nobility. Pick the terms: to first blood (a wound that bleeds, or with blunt weapons one of 4 or worse) or until one yields (pain of 0.35, 0.5 for the tough, 0.45 with bloodlust, 0.2 for a wimp, heavy bleeding, or down). They take it up at 45%, 10% for each step of temper, 2.5% for each level they lead at melee, 0.2% less for each point they regard the colony (more when they think ill of it), 10% more for first blood and 5% less to the yield, between 5% and 95%. Up to six of the colony nearby with nothing pressing and four of theirs gather round, and it is a real fight with their own weapons that stops at the terms; a fight still going after 4,000 ticks is a draw. Deaths are rare, but the game's own fight decides. A win gains 2 goodwill and one more for each of theirs watching (5 at most), their people remember it fairly won, and someone known by name thinks 8 better of the colonist (their notables watching, 5); a loss costs 1 goodwill, though the colonist earns 2 for standing up. The colony's watchers feel it for 3 days (4, or -2). With the deeper game hooks, their people don't count a duel's or a fistfight's blows as the colony attacking one of theirs. A bout waits 12 hours between the same two, hard words a day, and a duel ten days for the one challenged.
